one_liner: Twilio has a broad REST API with a free trial (no card) giving working Account SID/Auth Token credentials; Basic auth is primary, and a vendor-hosted, docs-only MCP server exists.
auth_notes: Main documented method is HTTP Basic using API key SID/secret or Account SID/Auth Token. OAuth 2.0 apps exist but are newer, so Basic/API key is safest primary. JWT Access Tokens are minted for client SDKs.
access_notes: Free 30-day trial, no credit card required, same credentials as upgraded accounts. Trial has restrictions (verified numbers only) but is enough to build and test. Upgrade is pay-as-you-go.
blocker_notes: No real blocker; trial accounts have messaging restrictions and expire after 30 days, but upgrading is self-serve.

evidence.quote: Twilio supports three authentication methods. Choose based on your security requirements and integration needs
"authentication": "Basic Auth with Account SID and Auth Token"
When you create a Twilio account, you start with a free 30-day trial that lets you explore Twilio products before upgrading.
